title: Enhancing Static Analysis for Practical Bug Detection: An LLM-Integrated Approach
reason: LLift combines path analysis with post-constraint guidance to feed an LLM for use-before-initialization (memory-safety) bug detection in the Linux kernel, reporting new confirmed bugs.

title: LLM-Assisted Static Analysis for Detecting Security Vulnerabilities
reason: IRIS uses an LLM to infer taint specifications and do contextual analysis over CodeQL taint paths for whole-repository vulnerability detection, quantified on CWE-Bench-Java against CodeQL.

title: LLM-IFT: LLM-Powered Information Flow Tracking for Secure Hardware
reason: LLM-IFT performs information-flow tracking on hardware (HDL) designs via LLM-driven intra/inter-module dependency analysis; unclear whether hardware RTL counts as code in scope and whether dependencies are structural input or LLM-generated.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
reason: General study of LLM confidence elicitation on commonsense/arithmetic tasks; no security analysis of code.

title: SV-TrustEval-C: Evaluating Structure and Semantic Reasoning in Large Language Models for Source Code Vulnerability Analysis
reason: Benchmark that varies data/control-flow complexity and applies structural/semantic perturbations to measure their effect on LLM vulnerability analysis of C code, with quantitative results.

title: Automatically Inspecting Thousands of Static Bug Warnings with Large Language Model: How Far Are We?
reason: Llm4sa extracts warning-relevant code via program-dependence traversal and gives it to an LLM to triage static-analysis bug/vulnerability warnings at scale (false-positive reduction).

title: GRACE: Empowering LLM-based software vulnerability detection with graph structure and in-context learning
reason: GRACE grounds LLM vulnerability detection in code graph structure plus retrieved in-context demonstrations; decision from title and known record, as the abstract was not returned by the APIs.

title: Can LLM Prompting Serve as a Proxy for Static Analysis in Vulnerability Detection
reason: Security-aware prompting with contrastive chain-of-thought and synthetic examples on partial code, with no structural program representation in the input.

title: LSAST: Enhancing Cybersecurity Through LLM-Supported Static Application Security Testing
reason: LSAST feeds SAST scanner results and retrieved vulnerability knowledge to a local LLM and reports that adding SAST context improves detection accuracy.

title: Vercation: Precise Vulnerable Open-Source Software Version Identification Based on Static Analysis and LLM
reason: Vercation combines program slicing with an LLM to isolate vulnerability-relevant code from patches and identify vulnerable OSS versions, reporting 93.1% F1.

title: Sanitizing Large Language Models in Bug Detection with Data-Flow
reason: LLMSAN makes the LLM emit data-flow paths and validates them with parsing-based program-property checks to sanitize false positives in bug detection, including Android malware apps.

title: Hybrid Automated Program Repair by Combining Large Language Models and Program Analysis
reason: GiantRepair is general automated program repair on Defects4J, not a security-analysis task.

title: LLMSmartSec: Smart Contract Security Auditing with LLM and Annotated Control Flow Graph
reason: LLMSmartSec grounds smart-contract vulnerability detection and fixing in a GPT-4-annotated CFG, but the abstract reports no quantitative result.

title: ProveRAG: Provenance-Driven Vulnerability Analysis With Automated Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
reason: ProveRAG retrieves web data to analyse CVE records for mitigation; the LLM does not analyse code.

title: VulScribeR: Exploring RAG-based Vulnerability Augmentation with LLMs
reason: VulScribeR uses RAG-based LLMs to generate vulnerable samples for augmenting deep-learning detectors' training data; the LLM does not perform the security analysis.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Integrated Large Language Models in Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
reason: RAG over a vector store of 830 known vulnerable contracts grounds GPT-4 smart-contract vulnerability detection, with quantitative success rates.

title: When GPT Meets Program Analysis: Towards Intelligent Detection of Smart Contract Logic Vulnerabilities in GPTScan
reason: GPTScan combines GPT with static analysis (key variable/statement recognition validated by static confirmation) for smart-contract logic vulnerability detection, with precision/recall reported.

title: Do Language Models Learn Semantics of Code? A Case Study in Vulnerability Detection
reason: Fine-tuned code transformers are given bug-semantics annotations (potentially vulnerable statements, buggy paths) as input, improving vulnerability detection F1 in 11 of 16 settings.

title: Software Vulnerability Detection with GPT and In-Context Learning
reason: VUL-GPT retrieves similar code and its vulnerability information (BM25/TF-IDF) as in-context grounding for GPT vulnerability detection, with experimental results.

title: TaintP2X: Detecting Taint-Style Prompt-to-Anything Injection Vulnerabilities in LLM-Integrated Applications
reason: TaintP2X runs static taint analysis from LLM outputs to sensitive sinks in application code and uses an LLM to prune false positives; it analyses app code rather than attacking agent loops, so E3 does not apply (boundary case).

title: Explainable Recommendation of Software Vulnerability Repair Based on Metadata Retrieval and Multifaceted LLMs
reason: Retrieves CWE/CVE knowledge-base context for vulnerable code snippets to ground LLM vulnerability repair, evaluated across 100 experiments.

title: ReCode: Improving LLM-based Code Repair with Fine-Grained Retrieval-Augmented Generation
reason: ReCode is retrieval-augmented general code repair (algorithmic bugs), not a security task.
